abstractio-formalis.definition: Abstraction of the intelligible form or mathematical nature (quantity/extension) from sensible matter.

abstractio-intuitiva.definition: Hoenen's technical designation for the intellectual operation in which the mind directly intuits universal, necessary formal relationships (such as spatial continuity and geometric properties) within the concrete sensible phantasm.

agere-sequitur-esse.headword: agere sequitur ad esse in actu
agere-sequitur-esse.definition: Classical Thomistic metaphysical axiom affirming that no causal agency or operation can proceed except from an entity that already possesses actual existence (esse in actu).

occurrences.display: agere sequitur ad esse in actu
agere sequitur (i. e. praesupponit) ad esse in actu

aisthema.definition: In Aristotle's De Anima (III, c. 8, 432a), the content of sensory perception from which the imagination forms phantasms and the intellect abstracts intelligible species.

aitema.definition: In Aristotle and Euclid, a demonstrable or constructible principle requested from the learner without proof within the science.

aiteo.definition: Aristotle's verb (Anal. Post. I 10, 76b28) for assuming a principle when the learner has no prior opinion or holds a contrary opinion.

anairei.definition: Plato's term in Republic VII (533c) for the dialectical method, which 'destroys' or transcends the provisional hypotheses of the mathematical sciences in order to ascend to the unhypothetical first principle.

andererseits.definition: Correlative discourse marker used in German mathematical exposition (paired with einerseits) when contrasting dual axiomatic or geometric aspects.

anordnung.definition: Hilbert's second group of geometric axioms (Axioms of Order / Betweenness) in Grundlagen der Geometrie.

apotheosis-of-stupidity.definition: G. H. Hardy's characterization (Mind, 1929) of reducing mathematical proof to purely mechanical, uncomprehending symbol manipulation.

approximationsmathematik.definition: Felix Klein's term for empirical/applied mathematics bounded by a threshold of sensory accuracy (limen exactitudinis), contrasted with Präzisionsmathematik.

arche.definition: In Aristotle and Plato, the foundational starting point of being, demonstration, or cognition (such as the unhypothetical principle in Republic VI–VII or the immediate premises of science in Posterior Analytics).

ars-epsilontica.definition: Weierstrassian rigorous limit and approximation analysis using arbitrary small quantities ε.

atomon.definition: An indivisible magnitude or unit lacking further division.

axioma.definition: Self-evident first principle that every learner must possess to acquire scientific knowledge (Aristotle, Anal. Post. I 2 & I 10).

beschaffenheit.definition: Term used by German mathematicians (such as Killing and Klein) to denote the intrinsic spatial or structural character of geometric figures and manifolds.

betweenness.definition: Fundamental order relation among collinear points (B lies between A and C), introduced by Pasch and formalized by Hilbert and Russell.

bezeichnungsweise.translation: Mode of designation / system of notation
bezeichnungsweise.definition: In modern axiomatics and mathematical formalism, a symbolic notation or convention for designating geometric objects and relations.

cheminement-de-la-pensee.definition: Émile Meyerson's phrase (1931) for the actual cognitive movement of the mind in scientific discovery and deduction.

circulus-vitiosus.definition: Circular reasoning or definition where the definiendum is presupposed in the definiens.

cogito-ergo-sum.definition: Descartes' existential judgment; analyzed by Hoenen in Appendix as an intuitive perception of a necessary connection between an experienced act (cogito) and existence (sum).

das-gedachte.translation: That which is thought / the object of thought
das-gedachte.definition: In Gerhard Stammler's epistemology of logic, the objective conceptual content grasped by the mind in judgment and inference, as opposed to mere psychological acts.

das-system-beider-punkte.definition: David Hilbert's phrase in Grundlagen der Geometrie (§ 1) designating a pair of points as determining a straight line in his axiomatic incidence relations.

denkgesetze.definition: In 19th- and early 20th-century German logic and epistemology, the fundamental normative principles governing valid conceptual thought and inference.

dispositio-rei.translation: Disposition / objective arrangement of the thing
dispositio-rei.definition: In St. Thomas Aquinas (Metaphysics IX, lect. 11), the real ontological arrangement of a state of affairs to which the intellect's composition or division must correspond for truth.

distinguo.definition: Classic scholastic disputation operator separating the true and false senses of an ambiguous thesis.

doctrine-prealable.definition: Ferdinand Gonseth's epistemological term for the pre-axiomatic intuitive body of knowledge that necessarily precedes and guides formal axiomatization.

dynamis.definition: Aristotelian potentiality, contrasted with actuality (energeia / entelecheia).

einerseits.definition: Correlative German expression used in mathematical analysis to distinguish complementary aspects of a geometric definition or postulate.

elektron.definition: Classical Greek term for amber, cited by Aristotle in Meteorology IV (388b) as a homogeneous natural substance and contrasted with modern microphysical particles.

energeia.definition: Aristotle's core metaphysical term for actuality or operation, originally derived from local motion and extended to all existential and cognitive acts.

entelecheia.definition: Aristotle's term for realized form or act as holding its end/completeness within itself.

epharmozomenou-tou-trigonou.definition: Euclid's phrase in Elements I.4 for the superposition of one triangle upon another.

epipedos-epiphaneia-estin.headword: ἐπίπεδος ἐπιφάνειά ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου ταῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς εὐθείαις κεῖται
epipedos-epiphaneia-estin.translation: A plane surface is that which lies evenly with the straight lines on itself
epipedos-epiphaneia-estin.definition: Euclid's Definition 7 of Book I (ed. Heiberg I, pp. 2–3).

occurrences.display: ἐπίπεδος ἐπιφάνειά ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου ταῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς εὐθείαις κεῖται

episteme.definition: Demonstrative knowledge through necessary causes and first principles.

ere-de-la-rigueur-de-weierstrass.headword: l'ère de la rigueur de Weierstrass
ere-de-la-rigueur-de-weierstrass.definition: Henri Poincaré's characterization of late 19th-century mathematical analysis, in which Karl Weierstrass replaced naive spatial intuition of continuous curves with rigorous epsilon-delta arithmetic definitions.

occurrences.display: l'ère de la rigueur de Weierstrass

erklaerungen.definition: David Hilbert's heading at the opening of Grundlagen der Geometrie introducing the primitive undefined domains of points, straight lines, and planes.

eutheia-gramme-estin.headword: εὐθεῖα γραμμή ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου τοῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς σημείοις κεῖται
eutheia-gramme-estin.translation: A straight line is a line which lies evenly with the points on itself
eutheia-gramme-estin.definition: Euclid's Definition 4 of Book I (ed. Heiberg I, pp. 2–3).

occurrences.display: εὐθεῖα γραμμή ἐστιν, ἥτις ἐξ ἴσου τοῖς ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς σημείοις κεῖται

facio-ergo-materia-rei-factibilis-adest.headword: facio ergo materia rei factibilis adest
facio-ergo-materia-rei-factibilis-adest.translation: I make/act upon it, therefore the matter of the makeable thing is present
facio-ergo-materia-rei-factibilis-adest.definition: Hoenen's formulation of the existential judgment of external material reality grounded in conscious bodily action upon matter.

occurrences.display: facio ergo materia rei factibilis adest

folium-moebii.definition: The non-orientable one-sided surface discovered by A. F. Möbius (1858), analyzed by Hoenen in Caput III § 2.4 to refute objections against defining surfaces as boundaries of bodies.

grenzprozess.definition: Passage to the ideal mathematical limit from empirical approximations.

ho-to-poson-gignosketai.translation: That by which quantity is known
ho-to-poson-gignosketai.definition: Aristotle's definition of the unit or measure in Metaphysics X (c. 1, 1052b20): the primary measure by which quantitative magnitude or multitude is cognized.

hoc-movetur-ergo-aliud-movens-existit.headword: hoc movetur ergo aliud, movens, existit
hoc-movetur-ergo-aliud-movens-existit.translation: This moves, therefore another (a mover) exists
hoc-movetur-ergo-aliud-movens-existit.definition: Existential causal inference from perceived motion to an existing efficient cause.

occurrences.display: Hoc movetur ergo aliud, movens, existit

hoc-movetur-ergo-locus-est.translation: This moves locally, therefore place exists
hoc-movetur-ergo-locus-est.definition: Existential inference from local motion (translation) to the reality of spatial location.

occurrences.display: hoc movetur localiter ergo locus est

homologia.definition: Plato's term (Republic VII 533c) for unexamined hypotheses accepted merely by convention.

hyle-noete.definition: Aristotle's term (Metaphysics VII 10, 1036a9; VIII 6, 1045a34) for pure spatial extension considered in the imagination apart from sensible qualities.

hyparchein.translation: To belong to / To exist / To inhere
hyparchein.definition: Aristotelian logical and ontological verb for predicate inherence or actual existence.

hypothesis.definition: In Aristotle (Anal. Post. I 2 & I 10), an assumed principle asserting that the subject exists or does not exist.

hypotithemai.translation: He supposes / assumes as a hypothesis
hypotithemai.definition: Aristotle's verb (Anal. Post. I 10, 76b28) for assuming a demonstrable proposition that seems probable to the learner.

in-actu-exercito.translation: In the exercised act (implicitly in performance)
in-actu-exercito.definition: Knowledge or principle grasped and used directly within the living act of thinking or perceiving, prior to explicit reflexive formulation (in actu signato).

in-actu-signato.definition: Explicit, reflexively thematicized statement of a concept or principle previously grasped in actu exercito.

insieme.definition: Mathematical set (used for the set/continuum of real numbers).

kinesis.definition: In Aristotle (Physics III 1), the actuality of what is in potentiality insofar as it is in potentiality.

kritzelige-kurven.definition: Felix Klein's vivid description (in Elementarmathematik vom höheren Standpunkte) of rough, imprecise empirical curves drawn by hand, contrasted with idealized analytic curves.

limen-exactitudinis.definition: The finite limit of precision inherent in all external sensory perception and measurement (Felix Klein).

logica-docens.definition: The explicit scientific theory of logical rules and syllogistic forms.

logica-utens.definition: Logic actively practiced by the mind in reasoning about objects (in actu exercito).

materia-intelligibilis.definition: Continuous spatial extension grasped in the phantasm apart from sensible qualities, serving as the principle of individuation and constructibility for geometric figures.

materia-sensibilis.definition: Physical matter endowed with sensible qualities (color, heat, weight, hardness), abstracted from in mathematics.

minimum-imaginabile.definition: Empiricist thesis (Berkeley, Hume) claiming imagination consists of finite indivisible minima.

minimum-visibile.definition: The smallest angular or spatial extent discernible by the eye.

moveri-sequitur-esse.definition: Scholastic principle expressing the necessary existential connection between motion and actual existence.

movetur-ergo-est.definition: Hoenen's primary paradigm (Appendix § 1) of an intuitive existential judgment connecting perceived motion with actual existence.

noesis.definition: Direct intellectual apprehension of intelligible natures and first principles in the phantasm.

nous.definition: In Aristotle (Anal. Post. II 19), the intuitive intellectual faculty that grasps immediate first principles.

omne-agens-agit-propter-finem.translation: Every agent acts for an end
omne-agens-agit-propter-finem.definition: Foundational Aristotelian-Thomistic principle of finality, cited by Hoenen as an existential synthetic judgment connecting causal action with teleological determination.

ou-meros-outhen.translation: That of which there is no part
ou-meros-outhen.definition: Euclid's Definition 1 of a point (Σημεῖόν ἐστιν, οὗ μέρος οὐθέν).

peras.definition: Aristotle's and Euclid's ontological category for surfaces, lines, and points as indivisible boundaries of continua.

phantasma.definition: Sensory/imaginative representation in which the intellect beholds universal mathematical and philosophical natures.

physis.definition: In Aristotle's Posterior Analytics and Metaphysics, that which is prior or more intelligible 'by nature' (φύσει / secundum naturam) as opposed to what is prior 'to us' (πρὸς ἡμᾶς / quoad nos).

poiountes-gignoskousin.definition: Aristotle's dictum (Metaphysics IX 9, 1051a31) that geometric truths become manifest by actively drawing and dividing figures.

pos-estin.translation: How it is / the mode of its being
pos-estin.definition: Aristotle's question in Physics IV regarding the ontological mode of existence of entities such as place, time, and the mathematical continuum.

praezisionsmathematik.definition: Felix Klein's term for pure, exact mathematics operating with idealized limits, contrasted with Approximationsmathematik.

pragma.translation: Thing / objective reality / state of affairs
pragma.definition: In Aristotle's logic and metaphysics, the extramental reality or objective state of affairs that grounds the truth of spoken and mental propositions.

prealable.definition: In French philosophy of mathematics (Gonseth, Poincaré), designating the intuitive cognition that must precede formal axiomatic construction.

principium-individuationis.definition: That whereby multiple individuals of the same species are numerically distinct (intelligible matter in geometry).

propositio-per-accidens.definition: A judgment joining subject and predicate through contingent coexistence rather than essential necessity.

propositio-per-se.definition: A necessary proposition whose predicate belongs to the intelligible nature of the subject.

prouparchein.definition: Technical peripatetic verb (used by Aristotle, Themistius, and Simplicius) signifying that the moving cause, mobile subject, or first principles must actually exist prior to motion or demonstration.

psyche.definition: In Plato and Aristotle, the vital and cognitive principle whose intellectual faculty (νοῦς) beholds mathematical and metaphysical truths.

rhysin-tou-semeiou.headword: ῥύσις τοῦ σημείου (acc. ῥύσιν τοῦ σημείου)
rhysin-tou-semeiou.definition: Ancient Greek kinematic conception (reported by Aristotle in De Anima I, 4 and Proclus) according to which the motion or flowing of a point generates a line.

rigueur.definition: Logical and deductive exactness in mathematical demonstration, central to the debate between Poincaré, Klein, and the formalist/logicist schools.

sachverhalt.definition: In German phenomenology and epistemology (Brentano, Geyser, Stammler), the objective relational structure in reality corresponding to a true judgment.

strecke.definition: Hilbert's term in Grundlagen der Geometrie for a bounded straight segment AB defined as the system of two points.

syngenes.translation: Kindred / connatural / of the same genus
syngenes.definition: In Plato's Republic VII and Aristotle's Posterior Analytics, the affinity and structural kinship of the mathematical sciences and their principles.

ta-ex-aphaireseos.definition: Aristotle's standard technical designation for mathematical entities abstracted from sensible qualities.

telos.definition: The goal or terminal perfection toward which an action or motion tends.

termini-significativi.definition: Terms possessing real intensional meaning and reference to intelligible objects, contrasted by Hoenen with the empty uninterpreted symbols of pure formalism.

termini-transcendentes.definition: Terms such as ens (being), unum (one), res (thing), and aliquid (something) that transcend the ten Aristotelian categories.

thesei.definition: In Aristotle's distinction between arithmetic and geometry: whereas the arithmetic unit is without position (ἄθετος), the geometric point is an indivisible having position (θέσιν ἔχον / θέσει).

thesis.definition: In Aristotle's Posterior Analytics (I, c. 2, 72a14), an immediate principle of demonstration that cannot be proved but is not indispensable for learning everything (divided into hypotheses and definitions); in geometry, spatial position.

ti-estin.definition: Aristotle's question of essential definition, distinguished from whether a thing exists (εἰ ἔστιν).

tithemenou-tou-semeiou.definition: Greek genitive absolute describing the constructive positing of a geometric point in spatial intuition.

tode.definition: Aristotle's expression for a determinate, demonstratively indicated individual entity.

umgekehrt.definition: Mathematical and logical term designating the converse of a proposition or geometric relation.

utopie.definition: Felix Klein's characterization of the claim that pure formal logic can generate mathematical science without any appeal to spatial intuition.

verknuepfung.definition: Hilbert's first group of geometric axioms (Axiome der Verknüpfung / Axioms of Incidence) in Grundlagen der Geometrie.

zusammenhang.definition: In German philosophy of mathematics (Hilbert, Klein, Stammler), the necessary structural interconnection linking axioms, concepts, and geometric configurations.
